svg.title: Diabetes in pregnancy split by when the high glucose starts: pre-existing type 1 or 2 diabetes (planned before conception, then managed trimester by trimester) causes malformations, while gestational diabetes found on the 24-28 week screen does not; a gestational diabetes that does not clear after delivery was type 2 all along; each column gives risks, numbered checks and treatment in order

svg.text: Diabetes in pregnancy: was the glucose high BEFORE organogenesis?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: organogenesis runs weeks 3–16, often before she knows she is pregnant

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: glucose goals for EVERY one: fasting < 5.3 · 1 h after meals < 7.8 mmol/L

svg.text: Found at 24–28 weeks: SCREEN every pregnancy

svg.text: 1 · 50 g glucose, any time of day, 1 h: < 7.8 normal, stop · ≥ 11.1 = gestational

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 2 · 7.8–11.0 → FASTING 75 g test: GDM if ANY of fasting ≥ 5.3, 1 h ≥ 10.6, 2 h ≥ 9.0
